items.title: Rent and wallet spends don't earn you a fee waiver
items.summary: Rent, wallet, utility, government, EMI and cash transactions no longer count towards the spending target that gets your annual fee refunded. You need that much more genuine shopping to get the waiver.

items.title: Insurance, gold, fuel no longer count for fee waiver
items.summary: Spends on insurance, gold and fuel stopped counting towards the annual fee waiver target on these premium cards, so hitting the waiver is harder. Rent, wallet, utility, government, EMI and cash spends were already excluded.

items.title: 1% fee on fuel spends over Rs 50,000 a month
items.summary: If your petrol and diesel spends cross Rs 50,000 in a statement cycle, Axis charges 1% plus GST on them. Below that, no fee applies.

items.title: 1% fee on gaming spends over Rs 10,000 a month
items.summary: Spending Rs 10,000 or more on online skill-based gaming platforms in one statement cycle now costs 1% plus GST. Below that threshold nothing is charged.

items.title: 1% fee on school fees paid via apps
items.summary: Paying tuition or school fees through third-party apps now costs 1% plus GST on every transaction. Paying the institution directly on its own website or card machine stays free.

items.title: 1% fee on utility bills over Rs 25,000 a month
items.summary: Electricity, water and similar bills totalling Rs 25,000 or more in a statement cycle now attract a 1% plus GST charge. Under Rs 25,000 in a cycle, there is no fee.

items.title: 1% fee on wallet loads over Rs 10,000 a month
items.summary: Loading Paytm-type wallets with Rs 10,000 or more in one statement cycle now costs you 1% plus GST on those loads. Stay under Rs 10,000 in a cycle and nothing is charged.

items.title: No interest on over-limit loan EMIs from May 2026
items.summary: If you are revolving a balance, EMIs for an Over-the-Limit Instant Loan will stop attracting interest from 30 May 2026. All other billed EMIs still get charged interest.

items.title: Horizon card free for new Burgundy savings accounts
items.summary: The Rs 3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card is waived if your Burgundy Savings Account is opened on or after 1 July 2026. The waiver is at the bank's discretion and needs the Burgundy relationship maintained.

items.title: Magnus fee free for new Burgundy salary accounts
items.summary: You save the Rs 12,500 joining and annual fee on Magnus if your Burgundy Salary Account is opened on or after 1 July 2026. Axis can withdraw this at any time and you must keep the Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Extra Rs 100 if you miss minimum due twice
items.summary: Missing your minimum amount due for two cycles in a row adds Rs 100 on top of the normal late fee, and it repeats every cycle until you clear it. Paying at least the minimum stops it.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad now costs 1.5%, not 1%
items.summary: If you let a foreign shop or an overseas-registered website bill you in rupees, Axis now takes 1.5% plus GST of the amount instead of 1%. Burgundy Private, Olympus and Primus cards pay nothing.

items.title: Refunds on foreign spends cost you 3.5%
items.summary: When you return something you bought abroad, Axis keeps an extra 3.5% of the refunded amount. So a cancelled foreign purchase leaves you out of pocket.

items.title: Rent fee no longer capped at Rs 1,500
items.summary: The 1% charge on rent payments has lost its Rs 1,500 per transaction ceiling, so a large rent payment now costs 1% of the whole amount plus GST. Olympus and Primus cards are exempt from the fee.

items.title: Times Titanium forex fee jumps from 2% to 3.5%
items.summary: Spending abroad on the Times Titanium card now costs 3.5% of the transaction as a foreign currency markup instead of 2%. That is an extra ₹150 on every ₹10,000 you spend overseas.

items.title: IndiGo card perks fully switched off
items.summary: All features and benefits on the 6E Rewards IndiGo cards ended on 1 December 2025, and any 6E Rewards you had were converted to IndiGo BluChips on 1 November 2025. Existing holders have been moved to a different HDFC card.

items.title: Infinia now needs ₹18L spends a year to keep
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you must spend ₹18 lakh a year on your Infinia card, or keep ₹50 lakh in average balances with HDFC, to stay on the Infinia programme. Fall short and the bank can move you off the card and its benefits.

items.title: New 1.75% markup on rupee spends abroad
items.summary: If you pay in rupees at an overseas shop, website or an India-based merchant registered abroad, HDFC will now add a 1.75% markup on top of the bill. This applies to all such transactions from 15 May 2026.

items.title: Late fee up to ₹1,300 if you miss a Jumbo Loan EMI
items.summary: Missing or part-paying an Insta Jumbo Loan EMI now attracts a slab-based late fee plus GST, from ₹100 on small dues to ₹1,300 when you owe more than ₹50,000. It kicks in from 20 June 2026.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad gets costlier from 15 Jan 2026
items.summary: ICICI is revising the Dynamic Currency Conversion fee charged when you pay in Indian rupees at an overseas shop or to a foreign-registered merchant in India. Most cards will be charged 3.50% of the transaction, while Times Black pays 1.49%, Emeralde cards 2.00%, MakeMyTrip Travel 0.99% and Amazon Pay 1.99%.

items.title: BookMyShow perks need ₹25,000 spend each quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you only get BookMyShow benefits if you spent at least ₹25,000 on your ICICI card in the previous quarter, so light users lose the perk. For example, spending ₹25,000 between 26 December 2025 and 25 March 2026 unlocks the benefit for April–June 2026.

items.title: Cardless ATM cash withdrawal ends Feb 21, 2026
items.summary: RBL is shutting down IMT cardless cash withdrawals at RBL and non-RBL ATMs from 21 February 2026, so you'll need your debit card to take out cash. Until then the service still costs Rs. 20 per transaction, and that fee is not refunded if the transaction expires or is cancelled.

items.title: CASHBACK SBI Card benefits are being changed
items.summary: The benefits on your CASHBACK SBI Credit Card are being revised from 1 April 2026, so check what you'll actually earn before your next big spend. The notice links to the details rather than listing old and new values.

items.title: Only 60,000 points a month for statement credit
items.summary: You can no longer wipe out a big bill with points in one go — statement credit redemption is capped at 60,000 points per month. Air India SBI Signature and the two PhonePe cards are exempt from this cap.

items.title: Statement credit only in blocks of 4,000 points
items.summary: You must redeem points for statement credit in multiples of 4,000, so leftover points below that stay stuck in your account. PhonePe SBI Card PURPLE and SELECT BLACK are excluded from this rule.

items.title: BPCL card: spend Rs.1 lakh to skip the Rs.499 fee
items.summary: You now have to spend twice as much in a year to get the Rs.499 annual fee waived on the BPCL SBI Credit Card — Rs.1 lakh instead of Rs.50,000. Spend less than that and the fee stays on your bill.

items.title: Small unpaid bills now attract a late fee
items.summary: Missing payment on a small balance now costs you: dues over Rs.100 attract a Rs.100 late fee (earlier nothing was charged below Rs.500), and dues in the Rs.500–1,000 band jump from Rs.400 to Rs.500. Larger slabs stay the same.

items.title: PhonePe Purple card: monthly reward cap cut
items.summary: You'll earn fewer points each month on your PhonePe SBI Card PURPLE — the monthly cap on PhonePe spends drops from 1,000 points to 750 (just 250 for insurance), and online spends drop from 1,000 to 750 points. That's roughly a quarter to three-quarters less reward value per month.

items.title: PhonePe Purple: no points on tolls, jewellery, fees
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 you stop earning any reward points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school/college fees, and on utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app. Spending in these categories now earns you nothing.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: more spends earn zero points
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 tolls, gifts, jewellery, education fees, and utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app earn no reward points at all. Route these through the PhonePe app if you want points.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: reward cap halved online
items.summary: Your monthly reward ceiling on the PhonePe SBI Card SELECT BLACK falls sharply — online spends go from 2,000 points to 1,000, and PhonePe spends from 2,000 to 1,500 (only 500 for insurance). Big spenders lose up to half their monthly points.

items.title: Overlimit spends will cost INR 550 each time
items.summary: YES BANK is bringing back the overlimit facility, so a transaction that goes past your credit limit can go through — but it will cost you INR 550 plus GST each time. Watch your limit if you don't want the charge.

items.title: POP-Club fuel waiver limited to INR 100 a month
items.summary: On the POP-Club card, the 1% fuel surcharge waiver now only applies to fill-ups between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, and you can get back a maximum of INR 100 per statement cycle. Anything outside that band gets no waiver.

items.title: ATM cash withdrawal fee jumps to min INR 650
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES BANK credit card will cost you at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 from 15 June 2026. The 2.5% rate stays the same, so small withdrawals get much pricier.

items.title: Failed auto-debit now costs up to INR 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, the fee rises from 2% (min INR 450) to 2.5% (min INR 500), and the monthly cap jumps from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000 per statement. Keep enough balance in your account on the due date.

items.title: Foreign spends get costlier on most cards
items.summary: The forex mark-up on overseas and international online spends rises on several cards from 15 June 2026 — for example Select and Ace go from 2.75% to 3.50%, Reserv and YES First Preferred from 1.75% to 2.00%, and Elite+ from 2.75% to 3.00%. YES Private (0.50%), Marquee (1.00%) and FREO (3.40%) stay unchanged.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver band changes on most cards
items.summary: The transaction range that qualifies for the 1% fuel surcharge waiver is being redrawn per card — for most cards the old INR 400–5,000 band becomes INR 500–3,000, while Paisabazaar Paisasave moves from INR 500–3,000 to INR 500–3,000 and premium cards get INR 500–5,000. Small fills below INR 500 will no longer get the waiver on cards that earlier started at INR 400.

items.title: New INR 250 fee for paying by cheque at branch
items.summary: Dropping a cheque at a YES BANK branch to pay a card bill of INR 1,000 or more will now cost INR 250 plus GST. This charge did not exist before.

items.title: Paying your card bill in cash now costs INR 500
items.summary: Depositing cash at a YES BANK branch to pay your card bill of INR 1,000 or more will cost INR 500 plus GST instead of INR 100. Pay online instead and you avoid it entirely.

items.title: Replacing a lost card now costs INR 199
items.summary: Getting a new plastic card after losing or damaging it will cost INR 199 instead of INR 100. Eco-friendly and metal BYOC cards keep their existing fees.

items.title: Horizon card free with new Burgundy Savings A/c
items.summary: The ₹3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card is nil if you open a Burgundy Savings Account on or after 1 July 2026. The waiver depends on you keeping that Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Magnus fee waived for new Burgundy Salary users
items.summary: You save the ₹12,500 joining and annual fee on the Magnus card if you open a Burgundy Salary Account on or after 1 July 2026. Everyone else keeps paying ₹12,500.

items.title: Paying abroad in rupees now costs 1.5%, not 1%
items.summary: If you let an overseas shop or website bill you in Indian rupees, Axis now charges 1.5% plus GST on that amount instead of 1%. Burgundy Private, Olympus and Primus cards pay nothing.

items.title: Rent fee of 1% no longer capped at ₹1,500
items.summary: Paying rent on your Axis card now costs a flat 1% plus GST on every transaction with no upper limit, so big rent payments cost more than before. Olympus and Primus cards pay no rent fee.

items.title: Infinia now needs ₹18L spend a year to keep
items.summary: From 1 April 2026, HDFC will only let you keep your Infinia card if you spend ₹18 lakh in a financial year (primary + add-ons) or hold ₹50 lakh in average bank balances. Fall short and the bank can move you to a different card.

items.title: New 1.75% markup on rupee spends abroad
items.summary: From 15 May 2026, paying in rupees at an overseas merchant or an India-based merchant registered abroad will cost you an extra 1.75% of the transaction. This applies even though you never touched foreign currency.

items.title: Late fee on Insta Jumbo loan EMIs from June 2026
items.summary: If you miss or partly pay an Insta Jumbo loan EMI from 20 June 2026, a late fee plus GST kicks in, ranging from ₹100 on small dues to ₹1,300 when you owe over ₹50,000. Nothing is charged if the outstanding is ₹100 or less.

items.title: Government payments now counted as utility spends
items.summary: Government payments are treated as utility transactions, so they earn only the (usually capped) utility reward rate on your card. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: No reward points on rent or wallet top-ups
items.summary: Rent payments and loading money into e-wallets earn you zero reward points, so those spends are effectively unrewarded. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: Free airport lounge needs ₹75,000 spend a quarter
items.summary: Complimentary domestic lounge visits are earned, not given: you must spend ₹75,000 in the previous quarter to get access in the next quarter. Rent, government, education and EMI payments, fees and interest do not count towards that ₹75,000.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad gets a new fee from 15 Jan 2026
items.summary: From 15 January 2026 ICICI Bank charges a revised Dynamic Currency Conversion fee every time you let an overseas machine (or a foreign-registered merchant in India) bill you in rupees — 3.50% on most cards, 2.00% on Emeralde cards, 1.99% on Amazon Pay, 1.49% on Times Black and 0.99% on the MakeMyTrip Travel card. Always choose to pay in the local currency to avoid it.

items.title: Free movie benefit now needs ₹25,000 spend a quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 your BookMyShow offer is no longer automatic — you must spend ₹25,000 in the previous quarter to unlock it for the next quarter. Spend less and you get no movie benefit that quarter.

items.title: Cardless ATM cash withdrawal being scrapped
items.summary: From 21 February 2026 you can no longer pull cash from RBL or other ATMs using IMT cardless withdrawal, so you'll need your debit card. The Rs. 20 per transaction fee for the service goes away along with the service itself.

items.title: Monthly limit on cashing in reward points
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can convert only 60,000 reward points a month into statement credit, so large point balances take longer to use up. Air India SBI Signature and both PhonePe SBI cards are not affected.

items.title: Points redeemed only in blocks of 4,000
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 statement-credit redemptions must be in multiples of 4,000 points, so leftover points below that stay stuck on your account. The two PhonePe SBI cards are excluded from this rule.

items.title: BPCL card: spend 1 lakh to dodge Rs.499 fee
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you must spend Rs.1 lakh a year on your BPCL SBI Card to get the Rs.499 annual fee refunded, double the earlier Rs.50,000. Spend less and you simply pay the fee.

items.title: Late payment now costs you on small bills too
items.summary: From 1 May 2026, missing a payment on a bill as small as Rs.100 will cost you Rs.100, where earlier anything up to Rs.500 was free. The Rs.500–Rs.1,000 slab also rises from Rs.400 to Rs.500.

items.title: No points on tolls, jewellery, fees on PhonePe cards
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI cards stop earning any reward points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school and college fees, and on utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app. These everyday spends will now earn you zero.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: reward caps halved
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI Card SELECT BLACK earns fewer points monthly — PhonePe spends fall from 2,000 points to 1,500 (500 on insurance), and online spends fall from 2,000 to 1,000. Anything above the cap earns you nothing.

items.title: Overspending your limit will cost INR 550
items.summary: YES BANK is bringing back the overlimit facility from 1 June 2026, letting transactions go through above your credit limit — but each one costs INR 550 plus GST. If you would rather not pay this, keep your spending inside your limit.

items.title: POP-Club fuel waiver limited to INR 1,000-3,500 spends
items.summary: From 1 June 2026, POP-Club cardholders only get the 1% fuel surcharge waiver on fills between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, capped at INR 100 per statement cycle. Fills below INR 1,000 or above INR 3,500 get no waiver.

items.title: Cash withdrawal on your card gets costlier
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES BANK credit card will cost you at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 from 15 June 2026. The 2.5% rate stays the same, but the minimum floor fee goes up.

items.title: Failed auto-debit fee jumps, cap rises to INR 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, the fee rises from 2% (min INR 450) to 2.5% (min INR 500) from 15 June 2026. Worse, the monthly cap on these charges goes from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000 per statement.

items.title: Forex markup rises on most YES BANK cards
items.summary: Spending abroad or on foreign websites gets more expensive from 15 June 2026 on several cards — for example Reserv and YES First Preferred go from 1.75% to 2%, Elite+ from 2.75% to 3%, and Select/Ace from 2.75% to 3.5%. YES Private, Marquee, FREO and BYOC rates stay unchanged.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver window changes on many cards
items.summary: From 15 June 2026 the transaction amounts that qualify for the 1% fuel surcharge waiver change by card — most cards move from INR 400–5,000 to bands like INR 500–5,000, INR 500–4,000 or INR 500–3,000, so small fill-ups under INR 500 no longer qualify. Paisabazaar Paisasave holders move from INR 500–3,000 to INR 500–3,000 range under the new table.

items.title: New INR 250 fee for paying by cheque
items.summary: From 15 June 2026, paying your card bill by cheque at a branch costs INR 250 plus GST if the amount is INR 1,000 or more. There was no such fee before.
